title: The Anatomy of Consciousness
coreMove: Treat attention as a limited organizing force and move it from scattered demands toward one chosen goal with feedback.
sourcePressure: The architecture chapter: attention is limited psychic energy, consciousness can fall into psychic entropy or order, and the self grows through differentiation plus integration.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Flatten psychic entropy into ordinary stress or make the chapter into focus-hack productivity advice.

sourceAnchors.name: attention as psychic energy
sourceAnchors.detail: the frozen heading index names attention as psychic energy in Chapter 2
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Attention behaves like a small current: whatever receives it starts shaping the day, and whatever loses it stops mattering in practice.

sourceAnchors.name: psychic entropy
sourceAnchors.detail: the frozen heading index names disorder in consciousness as psychic entropy
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Psychic entropy is what a split mind feels like when every open loop pulls on the same limited current.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm - a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

exampleSpecs.domain: a remote analyst with six dashboards open
exampleSpecs.audience: remote workers whose busyness hides fractured attention
exampleSpecs.stakes: the client forecast is due before noon and every tab claims urgency
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she drags five dashboards to a later folder, writes the one question the forecast must answer, and starts with the data column that gives feedback first
exampleSpecs.firstImage: At 8:17 a.m., Emily counts six open dashboards

exampleSpecs.domain: an emergency dispatcher after a chaotic shift
exampleSpecs.audience: operators and care workers who need order under pressure
exampleSpecs.stakes: a mistake in call priority can cost real response time
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he replays the shift and marks the moment his attention split between a radio code and a personal text, then builds a rule for the next call stack
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The radio hiss is still in Hugo's ear after midnight

exampleSpecs.domain: a chemistry student in a lab practical
exampleSpecs.audience: students who mistake concentration for willpower
exampleSpecs.stakes: one mislabeled vial ruins the trial and the grade
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: her lab partner asks what they are actually solving, and Rachel has to state the goal before touching the next pipette
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "What result are we trying to get first?"

exampleSpecs.domain: a youth football referee handling sideline noise
exampleSpecs.audience: people under public pressure who need a stable attentional target
exampleSpecs.stakes: the match is getting rough and parents are shouting over every call
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the sideline noise rises, he predicts he will miss the next offside unless he locks attention to the last defender, then tests it on the next attack
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The wet touchline shines under the floodlights

exampleSpecs.domain: a shop owner deciding whether to answer every customer review
exampleSpecs.audience: small business owners whose identity is pulled by criticism
exampleSpecs.stakes: one angry review could consume the morning and damage the inventory plan
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: you read the review twice, feel the self contract around it, and must choose between a defensive reply and the stock count that restores order
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You read the same one-star review for the second time

exampleSpecs.domain: a Toronto paramedic student building a simulation checklist
exampleSpecs.audience: trainees learning to order attention before live pressure
exampleSpecs.stakes: simulation errors are teaching habits that will travel into real calls
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show the messy first simulation beside the second run where he writes one cue for airway, pulse, and medication feedback before entering
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Yusuf needed one failed simulation to see the problem

skillTargets: choosing a goal that orders consciousness
distinguishing disciplined direction from rigid control

tryThisNowSpec: Pick the one open loop pulling hardest on your attention, write the next visible action it needs, and remove one competing cue from sight.
